Both are wider than the scan. Plants I, J and K pass the real test: a Set of numbers (bare, and inside a record with a source), and a figure in a record nested 10 or more deep, each with no status, are not seen. The cause is in tests/nexus/scans.ts, in both `unsourced` and `unstated`: `walk` returns at `depth > 8`, so nothing below depth 9 is read, and it handles a Map (`Object.fromEntries`) but not a Set (Object.entries of a Set is empty). The last verdict asked for exactly this: 'walk must count a number at any depth where no ancestor gives a status ... or the shapes must be named as not covered'. The Map and list-with-text shapes it named were closed; the 'any depth' it named was not (the cap of 8 stayed), and a Set was never walked. This is the third time the builder has closed the instance the evaluator named and not the class (a number held in a shape the walk does not enter).

No real record is affected today (independent probe: 0 uncovered of 5,093 numeric leaves, deepest at depth 4), so this is a blind spot, not a missing status. Needed: either walk Sets and descend past depth 8 (with a visited set against cycles instead of a depth cap), and plant a Set and a deep record in the test so a walk that stops seeing them is caught; or say in C21's row and in REALITY.md that a Set and anything nested below eight levels are not seen, and drop 'anywhere' and 'wherever it sits'.
